name: Kurdish (Sorani)
caution: 1.2 million words, versus hundreds of millions for the main languages. Frequency values are unreliable, so there are no frequency bands, only the all-words generators. The reference lexicon has 227,601 words, so generators, neighbourhood measures and cluster filters are rougher than for the main languages. Sorani Kurdish writes most vowels. CV here is orthographic: ا ە ۆ ێ و ی count as V; و and ی are also consonants (w, y), which this rule cannot tell apart. Latin-script (Kurmanji) entries in the source were dropped.

source: FILMS/OPUS subtitle frequency list: kurdish-ku/word/kurdish.ku.word.pron-one_col-default.filtered_by_pron.spell_checked.zipf_4.tsv; Leipzig Corpora Collection word list ckb_wikipedia_2021_100K (CC BY; Goldhahn, Eckart & Quasthoff 2012)

english_contamination_removed.rule: Leipzig-only words of 5+ letters that are English words with Zipf >= 4.5

reference_lexicon: plain words (alphabet only) with Zipf >= 2.0 and corpus count >= 3

model.trigram_variants: plain maximum-likelihood letter trigrams with two start markers and one end marker; type counts (each word once) or token counts (each word weighted by its per-million frequency)

filters.not_a_corpus_form: rejected if it occurs anywhere in the corpus word list
filters.phonotactic_legality: initial, medial and final consonant clusters and vowel sequences must each occur in >= 3 reference words

metrics.old20: mean Levenshtein distance to the 20 closest reference words
metrics.logprob: mean log2 probability per letter (incl. word end); model = generating model, all = all-words model

generation.target_rule: per generator and training set: 2 x the number of training words, between 5000 and 100000; a generator stops early when fewer than 1 in 20 recent samples is new and legal

multi_source.rule: a word found in only one of the 3 sources although 3+ occurrences were expected in the others (from its frequency) does not train the generators

cv_guess.method: letter-to-CV contribution table learned from IPA-annotated words (3-letter context with back-off), aligned by dynamic programming; evaluated on a held-out 20%
